key_insight: Interval-aware AI models predicted future subsolid pulmonary nodule growth and morphology from baseline CT across variable follow-up durations.
clinical_relevance: This imaging research—not drug discovery—may support personalized nodule surveillance, but clinical utility remains unproven.
method: Retrospective, single-center analysis of longitudinal CT scan pairs.
Discriminative model used baseline CT, segmentation masks, and interscan interval to predict growth.
Temporally conditioned generative model predicted future lesion morphology.
evidence_signal: Among 24,946 scan pairings from 2,543 nodules in 426 patients, test growth-prediction AUROC was 0.772 (95% CI: 0.704–0.818), and morphology Dice similarity was 0.706 ± 0.186.
watch_item: Performance declined at longer follow-up intervals; external validation is needed before clinical implementation.
paper_title: Prediction of Subsolid Pulmonary Nodule Evolution from Baseline CT Using Temporal Imaging Models
